cause_assessment.evidence_status: observed paired outcomes plus static design
cause_assessment.finding: Gains are concentrated in spaced acronym and question forms; lowercase quality is unchanged.
cause_assessment.interpretation: Consistent with the deliberate uppercase-acronym eligibility guard. This does not justify widening lowercase expansion after seeing this set.

cause_assessment.evidence_status: observed source/ranking outcome; causal explanation is inference
cause_assessment.finding: HTTP Server / Where is HTTP Server defined? still miss the HTTPServer definition in top five, while several returned snippets refer to HTTPServer.
cause_assessment.interpretation: Complete word occurrence is not definition identity. Original-form and lexical relevance can favor usages or nearby declarations; stored outputs do not expose the internal full candidate pool or branch trace.

cause_assessment.evidence_status: direct reconstruction from hit_ids, retained_ids and exact saved contexts
cause_assessment.finding: The 1024-token misses split between absent top-five source IDs and whole-source packing exclusions.
cause_assessment.interpretation: Packing misses are not a tokenization failure. The shared packer stops at the first whole block that does not fit; this is an evaluator boundary, not Book native token-budget assembly.

cause_assessment.evidence_status: observed repeated cost; operation attribution is inference
cause_assessment.finding: Spaced and question lookups are slower in all three repetitions; exact-name lookups are also slower without additional hit/top1/MRR gains.
cause_assessment.interpretation: The supplemental SQL and complete source-word verification are consistent with extra work. No profiler, operation trace or isolated causal experiment was run, so their shares are not quantified.

cause_assessment.finding: A 59.236313 ms lowercase candidate sample affects its mean.
cause_assessment.interpretation: The sample and all other tails are retained. Cause is unknown; neither removal nor an infrastructure explanation is justified.

cause_assessment.finding: Raw-code search reaches 43/44 hits in every form/budget and has lower recorded lookup latency.
cause_assessment.interpretation: The registered ordered compact-name-aware control is a strong control for this definition-location task. This result defeats a universal superiority claim; it does not measure persistence, multi-session memory, or full agent behavior.

limitations: Small single-repository identifier retrieval pilot; repetitions are correlated
Whole-source shared packing measures a component, not native end-to-end model response
Initialization, native lookup and IPC boundaries differ; no whole-product speed ranking
No model answers, generated patches, longitudinal real-user or universal superiority result
Four mechanically generated query forms per class are correlated; they are not 176 independent user tasks.
Three repetitions are repeated measurements, not three extra independent question sets.
All documents use one CPython revision/project; this does not test native multi-project, branch, time/as-of or longitudinal decision resolution.
Native Book recall used a 100000-character cap and no native exact token cap; 1024/4096 budgets are applied by the shared packer afterwards.
Top1 and MRR are calculated before packing and consequently repeat across budgets; do not count them as independent budget gains.
No-memory is an empty-retrieval diagnostic, not a model-without-memory answer or patch baseline.
Timing is descriptive component lookup cost under the registered schedule, not a randomized end-to-end model speed gate.
All remaining source/exact-commit CI, packaging and published-install checks remain outside this analysis.
next_iteration_hypotheses_not_applied: Distinguish declarations from mentions using source-location or symbol provenance; validate on new repositories and task histories rather than tuning to these 44 names.

Measure why complete source-word checking costs more, then reduce repeated parsing with explicitly versioned derived metadata or another bounded operation reduction. Include storage/ingest/migration costs if an index is introduced.
Keep the lowercase misses as an explicit unresolved tradeoff; any new matching policy requires its own false-positive controls and a new frozen confirmation set.
Evaluate fixed-model engineering answers or valid patches, first-attempt success, total tool rounds, model tokens and elapsed completion time. This pilot cannot establish those benefits.

changed: Raw-text control prepares compact source names and compares the ordered compact query name; full token coverage is the second ranking criterion as registered
Negative unit fixture proves ServerHTTP cannot win over HTTPServer for HTTP Server queries
pre_score_correction.reason: Root pre-execution review found that the raw-text control used unordered token-set equality where the registered plan required ordered compact-identifier equality. Correct the comparator to the registered stronger literal-name order, and retain the original binding unchanged.

resource_limitations: No RSS, CPU, energy, total model usage, or agent-tool retry metrics were recorded; none are inferred.
Database bytes are recorded for Book only; missing competitor storage is not zero storage.
Initialization includes different ingestion/index/import boundaries, so these numbers are not whole-product startup rankings.
source_disclosure: Real source excerpts; automatically authored identifier queries; fixed artificial capture timestamp shared by all arms. No authentic user conversations, temporal claims, generated answers or patches.

A. HISTORY OF THE SOFTWARE
==========================

Python was created in the early 1990s by Guido van Rossum at Stichting
Mathematisch Centrum (CWI, see https://www.cwi.nl) in the Netherlands
as a successor of a language called ABC.  Guido remains Python's
principal author, although it includes many contributions from others.

In 1995, Guido continued his work on Python at the Corporation for
National Research Initiatives (CNRI, see https://www.cnri.reston.va.us)
in Reston, Virginia where he released several versions of the
software.

In May 2000, Guido and the Python core development team moved to
BeOpen.com to form the BeOpen PythonLabs team.  In October of the same
year, the PythonLabs team moved to Digital Creations, which became
Zope Corporation.  In 2001, the Python Software Foundation (PSF, see
https://www.python.org/psf/) was formed, a non-profit organization
created specifically to own Python-related Intellectual Property.
Zope Corporation was a sponsoring member of the PSF.

All Python releases are Open Source (see https://opensource.org for
the Open Source Definition).  Historically, most, but not all, Python
releases have also been GPL-compatible; the table below summarizes
the various releases.

    0.9.0 thru 1.2              1991-1995   CWI         yes

(1) GPL-compatible doesn't mean that we're distributing Python under

    GPL-compatible licenses make it possible to combine Python with

(2) According to Richard Stallman, 1.6.1 is not GPL-compatible,
